MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MAY 20, 2019

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045
  Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR RETZ.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR RETZ led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Pope, Romanelli, Retz, Persichina, Ciarolla, Bain

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  McCormick

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Daniel A-Haja, Senior Recreation Leader
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  APRIL 15, 2019

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL
  15, 2019.

  There being no objection, COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  Tony Campanella, 38 Harbor Sight Drive, provided letters to the commission regarding
  the Taber Grove project from neighbors. He stated that neighbors that he spoke to
  were unaware of the project and are opposed to the project.

  Mr. Campanella expressed his concerns with the soil, parking, and transients.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that this project was approved by the
  Homeowners Association and would not have proceeded without their approval of the
  project. He also stated that the Sheriff’s Department will be contacted to address the issue
  with transients.

  CHAIR RETZ suggested that neighbors expressing concern should review previous
  meeting minutes. Many of the concerns expressed may have already been discussed.
  The purpose of the park is to be a neighborhood block park to walk-through and not a
  destination park.

  CHAIR RETZ assured Mr. Campanella that the Commission will take his comments and
  letters received from neighbors into consideration.

  Item 7-B taken out of order

  7-B.  PROPOSED MASTER CITY STREET TREE LIST ADDITION

  Community Services Director Clark stated that an application was submitted to add the
  Chinese Elm Tree tree to the Master City Street Tree list. He explained that there a few
  throughout the City; they are a partly deciduous and drought tolerant tree.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
MAY 20, 2019
   Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Park and
  Activities Commission approve the addition of the Chinese Elm tree to the City’s Master
  Tree List.

  CHAIR RETZ stated that he has this type of tree on his property and it has many leaves
  fall and the root system is intense.

  A brief discussion ensued.

  Ms. Carrie Booth, 6 Hidden Valley, stated that she was not aware of the root issue. The
  trees can handle trimming. The existing trees were flat-topped for wire clearing and a
  branch narrowly missed their home.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER BAIN, Community Services Director Clark
  stated that SCE has no obligation to correct damage to trees after wire clearing.

  Ms. Booth stated that the Sycamore and Liquid Elm may also be an option. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that those two choices were added to the list and will
  provide a revised list to Ms. Booth since an old list was inadvertently provided to her.

  Ms. Booth inquired if she can have the tree pruned. Community Services Director Clark
  stated that if a property owner chooses to have it trimmed, notice and insurance naming
  the City as additionally insured would need to be provided.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN inquired about the City reviewing the Master Tree List to
  encourage planting of native trees since the PVP Land Conservancy works hard to bring
  native trees back to the community.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that she agrees with COMMISSIONER BAIN and
  suggested having the PVP Land Conservancy review the list and make recommendations.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that a request to add a tree to the list should be
  from a City perspective as opposed to due to one particular property.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  TABLE THE REQUEST TO ADD THE CHINESE ELM TO THE MASTER TREE
  LIST.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  STREET TREE REMOVAL APPLICATION

  Staff recommends that the Park and Activities Commission approve the removal and
  replacement of three Eucalyptus street trees located at #6 Hidden Valley Road at the cost
  of the applicant.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN
  made a motion to approve the removal of three Eucalyptus street trees located at #6
  Hidden Valley Road at the cost of the applicant.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PARK USE REGULATIONS REVISIONS

  Community Services Director Clark stated that this has been brought back due to the Park
  Regulations Subcommittee recommending to change specific animals “… on a leash” to
  “pets on a leash”.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
MAY 20, 2019
   Community Services Director Clark stated that the Park and Activities Commission make
  a recommendation to City Council to amend Municipal Code Sections 12.24.020 and
  12.24.050.

  A brief discussion ensued.

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  AMEND MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 12.24.020, DELETING “UNLESS A PARK
  PERMIT IS OBTAINED ALLOWING SUCH ACTIVITIES OR ITEMS”; AND
  AMEND SECTION 12.24.050, DELETING THE FIRST SENTENCE. THE
  SECTION WILL READ AS FOLLOWS:

  “PETS MAY BE PERMITTED IN THE PARK IF THE SAME ARE KEPT UPON A
  LEASH UNDER THE FULL CONTROL OF ITS OWNER OR PERSON IN
  POSSESSION, INCLUDING THE PROPER DISPOSAL OF ANIMAL WASTE”.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA to

  CHANGE ITEM “E” IN MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 12.24.020 TO READ AS
  FOLLOWS:

  “REPETITIVE HITTING, KICKING, OR THROWING OF BALLS OR OBJECTS
  AGAINST PARK STRUCTURES”.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  8.  ADJOURN TO THE PEPPERTREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING

  The Park and Activities Commission adjourned to the Peppertree Foundation Advisory
  Board Meeting.

  A.  REVISED FOUNDATION LOGO

  Community Services Director stated that the logo sent from Tripepi Smith has not been
  revised.

  The following changes to the logo were recommended by the Park and Activities
  Commissioners:

  •  Show the horse walking on the trail or setback onto the hill as opposed to walking
  on the banner.
  •  Tree needs to be revised to more closely resemble a California Peppertree.
  •  The background go from beige to white and the trail go from white to beige.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that Daniel A-Haja will be tasked with following-
  up on this revision.

  B.  PV STREET FAIR & MUSIC FESTIVAL PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOOTH SIGN-
  UP SHEET

  COMMISSIONER POPE – JUNE 8 & 9 – MORNING
  CHAIR ROMANELLI – JUNE 8 - MORNING
  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA – JUNE 8 – MORNING
  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA – JUNE 8 - AFTERNOON

  C.  TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLES TOURNAMENT CONCESSION STAND SIGN-UP

  COMMISSIONER BAIN – JULY 21 - AFTERNOON

  D.  RACE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA stated that sponsors are confirmed.
PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
MAY 20, 2019
   CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the start time will remain the same. More advertised was
  discussed and there will be more effort made for youth support.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the bibs will be ordered from the vendor of
  prior years since last year’s bib numbers were too small.

  E.  TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLES TOURNAMENT SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE
  (VERBAL REPORT)

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the discussion was regarding the design of the t-shirt and
  a couple of more designs will be prepared and then a final decision will be made.

  9.  RECONVENE TO PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING

  The Park and Activities Commission reconvened to the Park and Activities Commission
  meeting.

  10.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMISSIONER BAIN provided the following issues to be addressed at Highridge Park:

  •  Drain blocked behind playground equipment
  •  Graffiti on the wall behind a property
  •  Restroom needs attention
  •  Soccer field grass
  •  Little Library doors do not close properly
  •  Little Library needs to be restocked with books.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the package for the restroom renovation
  project will be provided at the next meeting. The soccer field will be shut-down and re-
  seeded for new grass at approximately the end of May.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the Little Library at Rockbluff Park has been a target of
  vandalism and has been reported to the Maintenance Supervisor, who stated that is will
  be removed.

  CHAIR RETZ stated that the “Welcome to Rolling Hills Estates” sign needs to be repaired.
  This is the sign from Palos Verdes Estates into the City on Palos Verdes Drive East.

  11.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS

  A.  TABER GROVE SCENIC VIEW AREA EAGLE SCOUT PROJECT (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there is an Eagle Scout who will be
  installing the fence at Taber Grove scenic view area as well as a bench. He will bring back
  the design of the bench at a future meeting.

  B.  CITY CELEBRATION SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING – MAY 22, 2019 (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Director stated that the next City Celebration Subcommittee meeting
  will take place at the clubhouse on Wednesday, May 22nd.

  12.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 23, 2019

  Received and filed

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MAY 14, 2019

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
MAY 20, 2019
   Received and filed

  C.  PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF MAY 6, 2019

  Received and filed

  D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF APRIL 29, 2019

  Received and filed

  CHAIR RETZ commended Community Services Director Clark on his service to the City and
  congratulated him on his retirement.

  A retirement reception for him will take place in the City Hall Council Chamber on Tuesday, June
  11, 2019 at 6:00 p.m. with a formal recognition to follow.

  13.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  RE-NAMING “BUTCHER PARK”

  B.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH MEDIANS LANDSCAPING PROJECT

  14.  PARK TOURS

  The Park and Activities Commission proceeded to the Park Tours and provided the
  following items for replacement or repair:

  Peppertree Park

  •  No comments

  Chandler Park

  •  Broken and leaning rails

  Silver Spur Park

  •  Bury two irrigation pipes at entrance to the park
  •  Dead tree limbs need to be cut

  Rockbluff Park

  •  Top rails need to be repaired and painted
  •  Missing doggie bag dispenser at the bottom of the hill.

  15.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:46 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON JUNE 17, 2019 AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH WILL MEET
  AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK, 25851 HAWTHORNE BLVD., ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
  Administrative Assistant  City Clerk

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
MAY 20, 2019
